subject_line: Various performance improvements to parsing expr
s1_reason: parser.pegjs: removes PEG backtracking alternatives (X op Y / X) in pg_is_expr, pg_comparison_expr, pg_in_expr, comparison_expr, member_expr_or_func_call, dialect-guarded xor/collate rules; each failed alternative re-parsed the whole operand, exponential in nesting depth (issue #52: nested parenthesised AND/OR/= expressions, postgres "spun for over a minute")
s2_reason: cost depends on expression nesting depth and on how many precedence levels an operand passes through
s3_reason: grammar <or_expr>/<and_expr> recursion, comparison operators in <pred_expr>/<op_expr>, IN via <in_expr>, parenthesised compound primaries (two-tier rare <c_expr>) and qualified column refs (member_expr_or_func_call "." chains) generate exactly the #52 shape ((a.b=1) AND ((c.d=1) OR ...)). Runner engine=cst times cst.parse(sql,{dialect:postgresql}) plus JSON.stringify; changed rules are on the postgres expression path.
confounds: v0.21.2..v0.22.0 also contains ~40 commits of PostgreSQL DML support (UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/MERGE/INSERT ON CONFLICT) and breaking CST-type renames for those statements; none is reachable from the SELECT-only grammar. 5f5b4d8 makes YEAR_MONTH case-insensitive (MySQL). paren_less_func_call gained a !(__ "(") lookahead in afba66f itself. Both perf commits land in the same release, so the pair measures their sum.
notes: Listed in v0.22.0 release notes: "Fixed some serious performance regressions, especially when parsing PostgreSQL (#52)". Same release pair as 0596f1b. Issue says the slowness existed since 0.17.1 (pre-2024), so there is no in-window regression-introducing pair. Old version (0.21.2) predates some PostgreSQL SELECT support added later (e.g. 0.2x-0.4x additions), so more inputs will be rejected by the before side and dropped per pair at scoring.

s1_reason: pg_cast_operator_expr no longer parses member_expr_or_func_call twice when no :: follows (left-factored into optional right part)
s2_reason: every postgres operand passed through pg_cast_operator_expr was parsed twice on failure; compounded with nesting depth
s3_reason: every operand passes the cast level; grammar <cast_expr>/<cast_expr_rare> with <typecast> "::" <typename> produces the :: case, and all plain operands hit the formerly backtracking path. Timed region = cst.parse(postgresql).

Both perf commits land in the same release, so the pair measures their sum.
